A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AUTALIC and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.7. All 17 pages of each version support comparison, including matching retained figures and appendix analyses.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments in Table 3, human–LLM agreement in Figure 4, and annotation analyses, including the preliminary self-agreement study in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds an analysis of LLM classification errors in Section 4.4.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, annotation procedure, BERT fine-tuning, and zero-shot and in-context prompting procedures remain unchanged. Rewriting their descriptions does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,400 English-language Reddit target sentences and surrounding context for anti-autistic ableism classification. The added error analysis examines retained data without introducing a new task, population, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains logistic regression, pretrained and fine-tuned BERT, Gemma2, Mistral, Llama3, and DeepSeek in the corresponding comparisons. The new error analysis uses the existing LLM set.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds an error-analysis selection procedure described as examining the top 10% of sentences with unanimous human annotations but disagreeing LLM predictions. Existing train–test splits, metrics, prompts, and contextual inputs remain unchanged; the new subset's ranking criterion and prompting condition are not fully specified.

E4.justification: v4 adds a focused analysis of LLM over-classification, examining intra-community discussion, slurs, negative wording, and a quoted-viewpoint example in Figure 5. Earlier annotator-disagreement, prompt-sensitivity, and appendix self-agreement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing mean/standard-deviation summaries and correlation significance reporting remain unchanged. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported; the new cross-model percentage range describes outcomes rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: Section 4.4 newly reports 42 sentences labeled ableist by Llama versus zero by humans, with 74–93% also labeled ableist by other LLMs. It identifies 29 intra-community discussions, two sentences containing slurs, and 34 containing other negative wording. All five tables and the retained agreement plots preserve their earlier results.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. The retained classification definitions and statistical measures receive no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its consistency claim from reasoning LLMs generally to some LLMs, explicitly naming DeepSeek. The central claims about the first contextual anti-autistic ableism dataset, its scope, and LLM unreliability remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds an interpretation that negative wording can override contextual understanding and produce censorship of community discussion. v4 also qualifies several deployment conclusions with 'if deployed as-is'; the existing cultural, selection-bias, and language-evolution limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a project URL in the abstract and Appendix A.1.7, replacing the earlier redacted website reference. Its ethics statement explicitly extends the stated use prohibition to state actors in high-risk domains such as healthcare. No new training hyperparameters or hardware details are supplied.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged. The removed Devlin et al. (2019) entry duplicates the BERT work retained as Devlin (2018); other reference changes concern bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: Extensive prose rewriting affects the introduction, data collection, experimental results, discussion, conclusion, limitations, and ethics statement. Section 4 also receives a flatter subsection hierarchy, revised headings, and reordered discussion paragraphs.

P2.justification: v4 adds the error-example Figure 5, refines several captions, and reflows the document. Existing figure artwork and table structures are retained; the appendix's former Figures 5 and 6 become Figures 6 and 7.

improvement.justification: The added error counts and contextual example give concrete support to the censorship concern, while clearer organization and disclosed project access information improve usability. These are limited gains: the benchmark results remain unchanged, and the selected-error analysis does not establish overall false-positive rates or isolate negative wording as a causal mechanism.
